summary:
I've been building Keikochō, a Japanese-learning dashboard I coach myself with, and Finac, a gamified financial-literacy app for the family — both grew from the same architecture: curriculum-as-data, a Leitner box engine with recognition/production split, and a stage gate computed purely from a persistent log.

The interesting fight in Keikochō was around honesty of assessment. Early on I built a typed-recall placement test and watched myself stall three items in — I'm a true beginner, and typing romaji demands production I hadn't learned yet. I rebuilt it as tap-to-select with audio on every tile, and the scoring stayed honest about it: a quick unassisted pick promotes, but anything cued by the audio gets flagged and routed back into the teaching queue instead of counting as mastered. That distinction — recognition vs. real recall — ended up as a rule threaded through every later feature, right down to which drills are even allowed to count toward the gate that unlocks the next stage.

Adding card art turned into its own pipeline problem. I generate images through ComfyUI on a shared GPU, and about 5% of jobs time out under contention with other work queued on the same card; the fix was just making retries free — the generator skips any file that already exists, so "run it again" is the whole recovery story. Curating the output mattered more than generating it: the model kept confusing sibling concepts (red → strawberries instead of the color, seed → sunflower instead of "seed"), and a handful of prompts turned out fundamentally unimageable — raw meat cuts, abstract feelings — so I deleted those rather than ship a wrong picture. A missing image is safe; a wrong one teaches the wrong word.

Finac reuses that same engine but swaps in a different invariant, because real money is involved. Keikochō recomputes streaks and XP fresh from the log every time, which is fine when a correction can silently claw back credit. For Finac I made the ledger append-only instead — nothing is ever edited or deleted, only reversed by a new entry pointing at the original — because a balance you can quietly rewrite isn't one you can trust with actual dollars.

Smaller but real: chasing a bug on Keikochō's Stage-1 design, I used `0` as a sentinel for "session not yet started," which collided with the legitimate session number `0` and made items look permanently unseen. Rewrote it to use `None`. Small thing, but a good reminder not to reuse a valid data value as your "nothing here" marker.

highlights.oneLiner: Generating card art for an internal learning app; retries are free, skip-if-exists on timeout
